title: No Cover
description: A bare black record, sold without a sleeve, lying on a white table under one soft light. The grooves throw the light back as a narrow fan that turns as the light moves. Drag across the vinyl and you cut fine scratches that catch the light. Press and hold and the record spins up: the sheen streams, and every scratch you made clicks once a turn as it passes under the stylus, so the damage you did is what you hear.
intent: After Christian Marclay, Record Without a Cover (1985), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_Without_a_Cover: a record sold with no sleeve, so the scratches from handling become part of its sound. Here the wear is the instrument.
